subject: Trust Lattice & Operator Boundary Validation — BluePeak RFP follow-up
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: BluePeak Security <security@bluepeak.com>
Cc: Veritas Audit <auditor@veritas-audit.com>
Date: Tue, 19 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Trust Lattice & Operator Boundary Validation — BluePeak RFP follow-up

Hi Maya / BluePeak team,

Thanks for the RFP — attached is an initial evidence packet that addresses the specific trust and operator-boundary questions you listed: bluepeak-trust-lattice-diagram.pdf (network/trust-lattice diagram) and operator-boundary-evidence.zip (config snippets, KMS policy extracts, ephemeral access logs).

High-level summary (TL;DR):
- Trust lattice: control plane (management APIs, scheduler, model registry) runs in Redwood control VPCs isolated from the inference runtime VPCs. Communications between control and runtime are strictly mutual‑TLS authenticated over private peering links; service-level access is limited by per-route ACLs.
- Operator boundary model: operator/Admin actions (deploys, infra changes, debug sessions) are gated through our identity broker + ephemeral certificate issuance (short-lived certs via OIDC) and conditional access policies (SSO with device posture AND step-up MFA). No persistent shell access to inference hosts.
- Data plane isolation: inference workloads are constrained to customer-dedicated inference subnets when requested (Dedicated/Private modes). Egress is forced through tenant-specific egress proxies with allowlists; we support both NAT gateway and proxy-based egress filtering depending on deployment.
- Key management and crypto: customer keys (optional in Private) or Redwood-managed CMKs (Hosted/Dedicated) in KMS-backed HSMs. Per-tenant envelope encryption for model artifacts and KV cache.
- Audit & telemetry: write-once audit chain (signed, append-only), streaming to tenant-storage or customer SIEM via secure forwarders. We include sample audit traces in the evidence bundle.
- Supply chain attestations: images are signed; we publish SBOMs and provenance via Sigstore. We run CVE scans and produce attestations delivered with each release.

Please review the attached packet and let us know: (1) which items you want expanded into auditor-friendly artifacts, (2) whether you require control plane placement in your VPC (Private option), and (3) availability for a 45-minute call next week to walk the diagram and live proofs.

Next steps proposed:
1) We can produce an appendix with redacted audit traces and RTR captures for your Veritas team.
2) If you want per-region operator restrictions, we can show our deployment policy templates (region-scoped IAM + deny lists).

Attachments: bluepeak-trust-lattice-diagram.pdf (diagram), operator-boundary-evidence.zip (config & snippets).

Thanks,
Mateo Alvarez
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai

From: BluePeak Security <security@bluepeak.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 19 Jun 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Trust Lattice & Operator Boundary Validation — BluePeak RFP follow-up

Mateo —

Appreciate the packet and quick turnaround. A few clarifying items before we escalate to Veritas audit:
1) Operator sessions: can you confirm there is no out-of-band SSH jump host that permits interactive sessions directly on inference hosts? We need explicit guarantees about ephemeral console access.
2) Log retention: what is the default retention for operator audit logs in Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private? Does Redwood provide immutable retention buckets and the ability for us to export on demand?
3) Control plane in-customer: you mention Private option — does that mean control plane processes (or a slim control-plane proxy) can run in our VPC so API calls never traverse Redwood-managed control VPCs? If yes, what is the supported deployment model and SLA delta?
4) Evidence format: Veritas prefers CSV samples for audit traces plus a short README with field mappings. Can you include that?

We'd like to schedule the call early next week (PST) after we review the appendix.

Thanks,
Maya Jensen
Security Lead — BluePeak Analytics
security@bluepeak.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 21 Jun 2028 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: FW: BluePeak follow-ups — operator boundary clarifications (internal)

Mateo / Kim —

Quick internal: Maya's questions are straightforward but we should tighten a few artifacts before sending to Veritas:
- Confirm and document: no persistent/interactive SSH to inference hosts. We already run a bastionless model for most deployments; need a short note on auditability of ephemeral session broker (OIDC cert issuance flow + CA expiration times).
- Retention: default Hosted = 90 days (raw), 13 months (indexed, rolled to cold storage). Dedicated = configurable; typical customer commit 13/24/36 months. Private = customer-managed retention. We should provide the policy IDs and S3 lifecycle snippet in the appendix.
- Control plane in-customer: we support a Private Control Proxy — a slim control-plane proxy runs in customer VPC that authenticates to Redwood control plane and enforces tenancy rules locally. SLA differs; offer +99.5% for proxy-only (customer infra dependent) vs +99.9% standard. We should include the deployment diagram and operations runbook excerpt.

Action items:
1) Mateo — add CSV audit-sample and README to the evidence zip (audit-trace-sample.csv + audit-readme.txt).
2) Kim — assemble the retention policy snippets and the Private Control Proxy runbook excerpt.
3) I'll build a short slide appendix summarizing operator session hardening and the ephemeral cert flow.

Ben
Principal Security Architect, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Trust Lattice & Operator Boundary Validation — BluePeak RFP follow-up

Maya —

Thanks for the questions. Short answers and attachments are in the shared Drive link below; I've also attached CSV samples in the evidence bundle. Full appendix is here: https://drive.redwood.company/bluepeak/rfp-trust-lattice-2028

1) Operator sessions: explicit guarantee — Redwood does not permit persistent, unaudited SSH to inference hosts. Access patterns are:
   - Ephemeral certificate issuance via OIDC (short TTL, default 15 minutes).
   - All operator actions go through our admin API or via the operator console which requires device posture + MFA.
   - For debug/exfil trace, we use ephemeral session proxies that stream audit logs to append-only storage; session recordings are hashed and included in the audit chain.
2) Log retention:
   - Hosted: default 90 days hot, 13 months cold (customer can request extended retention).
   - Dedicated: retention is configurable per contract (we provide the lifecycle policy snippets).
   - Private: retention is controlled by the customer (we supply the policy templates).
   - All modes support export to customer S3/HTTPS SIEM endpoints; exports are signed and include a manifest for chain-of-custody.
3) Control plane in-customer: we support a Private Control Proxy model. Options:
   - Proxy-only (recommended for most customers): a small control-plane proxy runs in the customer VPC, authenticates via mTLS to Redwood control endpoints, enforces local policy and surfaces a minimal admin surface back to Redwood for telemetry and billing. SLA: +99.5% (customer infra dependent).
   - Full private control plane: full control plane components can be deployed in-customer under an enterprise license (on-prem or VPC). SLA and packaging are negotiated in vendor contract.

Attachments included in the Drive and evidence zip: audit-trace-sample.csv, audit-readme.txt, trust-lattice-diagram.pdf, operator-boundary-evidence.zip (config extracts, lifecycle policies, Sigstore attestations).

Next steps:
- I propose a 45-minute technical walk-through on Tue 2028-06-27 10:00 PST. Please confirm availability.
- We can package a Veritas-friendly appendix (CSV + README + short mapping doc) — Ben will drop the slide appendix and Kim will attach lifecycle snippets by EOD tomorrow.

DocSign link for the standard NDA (if you want the full Private control-plane SOW after call): https://docusign.com/ABCDEF-BluePeak-NDA

Regards,
Mateo Alvarez
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
